rule_findings.rationale: Material departures are not left implicit: each is written into the governing phase design and the parent design edit ships in the same change, and the artifact is itself re-entering the phase-design review boundary before dependent work advances — exactly the remediation the rule requires. Scope narrowing in Section 1.1 is permitted by the parent design's conditional wording ("may expose a narrow validation adapter if cutover needs one") and is verified against the repository: skills/archflow-constitution/SKILL.md contains no archflow-local or archflow_ reference, so no constitution adapter is owed. No implementation is authorized by this document ahead of its own approval.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: Section 10 pins that implementation may begin only after this exact phase design is independently reviewed, explicitly approved, committed through the authorized task-local milestone, and durable status advances to phase-impl-4. Section 1.3 discloses four material implementation-time deviations (main merge 54d60e9, dev-mode replacing self-cutover reinstalls, the unrestorable-missing-projection fix, host-proof digest binding) and folds them back into this governing document, with detail in phases/4/impl-notes.md; Section 1.1 records the constitution-adapter scope narrowing, and Section 4.2 step 4 corrects the parent task design's upgrade diagram in the same production change (Section 5.2 lists .archflow/tasks/api-refactor/design.md in file scope).

rule_findings.rationale: Every advancement point named by the phase remains bound to an explicitly recorded human choice for the exact subject: adoption is gated by the approved preview digest, the review boundary by the one migration-audit gate, and the import commit by that gate's acceptance. The single-confirmation import-milestone rule is not a new inference — it is the parent design's and PRD R8's stated distinction between implementation commits (explicit pre-commit confirmation) and milestone commits, and it is applied to a milestone, not to implementation. Retirement removes advertisement and handlers, not durable decision history (Section 3.1), so no existing authority record is weakened.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: Section 4.2 keeps two distinct explicit human decisions in the upgrade flow (preview approval bound to approved_preview_digest before stage; the migration-audit gate choice recorded through the existing decision-archive/decision-settle machinery) and makes migration-audit acceptance the import-commit authority with requires_human_confirmation: false under the established design-milestone rule, matching the pinned parent design's Section 3.5 upgrade text. Section 7 states that no acceptance test may infer approval, adopt an import without the staged approved preview, or create a commit without the exact durable authority the workflow already requires. Section 5.1 adds only a composeGate migration-audit arm over openDurableGate's existing deep validation, which the repository confirms is absent from request-composition.ts today.

rule_findings.rationale: Non-success states stay visible with a safe next action: blocked/inspect and fail-closed behavior are preserved, the degraded manual-status ladder survives retirement, and the newly discovered wedge is resolved by offering a client-reachable produce re-entry that re-declares the drift and deletion so the review boundary still covers the bytes. Section 1.1 and Section 4.2 step 4 correct the parent documents rather than quietly conforming to them, and Section 8 criterion 8 requires recorded host evidence instead of claimed capability.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: Section 1.3 discloses the mid-phase failure that falsified success criterion 5 for this very task (main-family durable records unparsable by this branch) and the wedge found while dogfooding (unrestorable adoption-sourced projection with no client-reachable action), together with the routing fix rather than a silent bypass. Section 4.2 step 5 keeps the degraded ladder ending in "stop and wait for the user to restore the server"; Section 5.4 requires tampered staged bytes to fail closed and crash cuts to converge; Section 4.3 has the status skill render open-gate presentations without resolving them; Section 4.6/8 make the real-host proof opt-in, auth-probed, and digest-bound rather than asserted.

rule_findings.rationale: The phase adds no cross-task read or write path: adoption is a task-scoped local transaction over already-staged bytes, and the new gate arm reuses the existing subject/evidence validation rather than composing new bindings. Retirement is limited to advertisement and handlers, so approvals, waivers, and review evidence continue to identify the exact task and subject bytes they govern, with mismatched or tampered evidence required to fail closed.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: Section 4.2 step 2 scopes adoption to `archflow-local upgrade adopt --task <task>` over the existing initialization transaction, with an unexpected staged-bytes mismatch failing closed; Section 4.2's closing paragraph and Section 4.5 pin the `--task <task>` requirement on every archflow-local snippet in the upgrade contract test. Section 3.1 and Section 7 keep durable vocabulary (TOOL_NAMES, gate archives, provenance channels) and existing approval bindings untouched, and Section 5.4 requires tamper and crash-cut coverage at the adoption and gate-archive/settle boundaries. The migration-audit arm derives from facts.migration_audit under openDurableGate's existing deep context validation (src/state/gates.ts).
